answer: Because the age is read from the beacon checkpoint rather than self-declared, the juniper audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm thus means funding each duplicate self through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. An identity must be at least 2 epochs old on the spiral ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 8 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
